newsitem.title: USA: India to seek 50,000 T optional origin wheat - trade.
newsitem.headline: India to seek 50,000 T optional origin wheat - trade.

text.p: India was scheduled to seek late Tuesday 50,000 tonnes or more of optional-origin wheat for March arrival, several U.S. exporters said.
"They (India) are supposed to be tendering for 50,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat but the quantity could be much bigger," one U.S. exporter said.
Exporters said they expect India to tender for hard wheat which could be from either Australia or the United States.
They added that India could be seeking up to 750,000 tonnes of wheat but shipping details were sketchy.
"It would be several different cargoes of 50,000 tonnes," a second U.S. exporter said.
Hard red winter wheat futures on the Kansas City Board of Trade firmed on Tuesday, partly supported by talk of U.S. export business, traders there said.

Kansas City traders said India would tender Wednesday for optional origin wheat after some Canadian wheat purchases reportedly did not meet phytosanitary requirements. Traders said India may have cancelled some of the Canadian purchases.

A spokesman for the Canadian Wheat Board early Tuesday said he was not aware of any quality problems regarding Canadian wheat being shipped to India. But he said he planned to check with shipping sources at the CWB.
"We are loading vessels for India and they are meeting all contract specifications," the spokesman told Reuters.
India's State Trading Corporation on Tuesday denied a report by the Statesmen newspaper that India had contracted to buy poor quality wheat from Canada without checking for levels of mycotoxin.
